## What to build

Every delegated task has a durable result file. A worker's `herdr-say --parent` first appends its report to its parent's results directory beside its hand-off log (`lanes/<lane>.results/<worker provider session>.md`, or `director.results/` for a director's own worker) (header: worker, role, lane or director, at), then sends the parent a notice naming that file and the report's first line. If the send is uncertain, queued or the parent is resumed, the file still holds the result, so nobody forwards it by hand and nothing is resent. `octo-feather-handoff results` lists the caller's outstanding workers (a spawn line in its log with no later attempt line for that session): name, pane, Herdr state, and the result file, or `ended, no result file` when Herdr no longer finds the worker and no file exists, a visible state, not silence. The supervisor role reads the listing on a wake, after compaction or a resume, in place of reading worker panes; that role change ships with its eval case.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] result files have one remover: `octo-feather-lane archive` moves the lane's results directory into `archive/` with the record and log; a director worker's file is removed when the director records that worker's attempt line (or the rule this ticket states, named in the spec call)
- [ ] demo: `scripts/octo-feather-handoff results` run as the supervisor after its worker's `herdr-say --parent`: lists that worker with its result file path

## What to build

Pilot, the lane's one ticket. Each `herdr-spawn` launch installs Herdr's Pi extension for itself alone: `herdr integration install pi` into a dir named by the launch's session under `$(octo-feather-state)` (beside its launch-set record), and Pi gets `--extension` on that copy. `octo-feather-lane stale` keeps marking a running agent stale when Herdr would now install a different extension (a Herdr upgrade): it compares the agent's recorded extension with what a launch would install now (a fresh install into a temp dir, or Herdr's integration version), never with the agent's own copy, which nothing rewrites.

A session's install dir ends when `herdr-close` closes (or parks) that agent's tab, after the close; a resume installs again. herdr-comms SKILL.md's Spawn an agent names the new place.
